entries.title: AI stocks climb after trillions wiped from market values
entries.snippet: Investors had been selling off tech shares in part due to concerns the Democrat election victory would mean slower AI development.

entries.title: Four midterms takeaways for 2028 White House race
entries.snippet: The buzz about the presidential election is already under way - here's what we learned this week.

entries.title: Two dead after bus crashes in France, officials say
entries.snippet: One child and one young adult were killed in the crash, local authorities say, with more injured.

entries.title: New wave of bomb threats hit European airlines
entries.snippet: No link has been established between the threats against the airlines and those against the media outlets.

entries.title: Kenyan doomsday cult leader given life sentence for murdering 191 people
entries.snippet: Paul Mackenzie ordered his followers to starve their children to death in a forest so they could "meet Jesus".

entries.title: Spain's rail authorities face European fraud probe after Urda rail disaster
entries.snippet: Prosecutors begin investigating EU funds meant for upgrading the Spanish railway line where a train crash killed 69 people.

entries.title: Judge blocks construction of Trump's massive arch after federal agency approval
entries.snippet: The Trump administration had hoped the construction of the 250-foot arch could begin as early as this week.

entries.title: Russian extremist group denies sending hoax bomb threats
entries.snippet: Scores of flights across Europe have received bomb threats this week, but no explosives have been found so far.

entries.title: Pope begins lengthy trip to Latin America weeks after lung cancer surgery
entries.snippet: Pope Leo, who had part of a lung removed last month, will visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru.

entries.title: Dozens of Democrats eyeing 2028 presidential run, says former Obama aide
entries.snippet: Jim Messina tells the BBC that after Democrats' midterm victories he's talked to "over two dozen campaigns", with some already hiring staff.

entries.title: Tanzanian opposition leader found guilty of inciting unrest but acquitted of treason
entries.snippet: The 58-year-old, who has been detained since April last year, says the charges are politically motivated.

entries.title: Elon Musk appears to signal the end of the road for Cybertruck
entries.snippet: Musk said it was to make room for production of its Cybercabs - autonomous taxis without a driver.

entries.title: Somalia's top court rejects president's term extension amid political crisis
entries.snippet: The country's first nationwide elections since 1969 are due next year - a timetable now thrown into doubt.

entries.title: Major construction ongoing near Iran missile bases, satellite images suggest
entries.snippet: Evidence of digging and new buildings are visible in satellite imagery taken in November, satellite images suggest.

entries.title: California governor commutes sentences for state's 548 death row inmates
entries.snippet: California has historically had the largest population of people on death row in the US.

entries.title: Nigerian court rules opposition candidate cannot stand in elections
entries.snippet: The high court has sacked the leadership of the opposition ADC party with only months to go until elections.

entries.title: Macau jails pro-democracy campaigner in city's first national security case
entries.snippet: Au Kam San was sentenced to 12 years and six months' jail for "subversion against the political power of the state".

entries.title: Paraguay President Santiago Peña resigns after bank collapse
entries.snippet: The move follows a bank collapse and after the lower house of congress voted in favour of pursuing an impeachment trial against him.

entries.title: Watch: Is it the end of the road for Tesla's Cybertruck?
entries.snippet: The car company's CEO Elon Musk has said production will halt in Texas, to focus on the firm's self-driving Cybercabs.

entries.title: Bomb hoaxes: Messages reveal how threat was passed on by air traffic control
entries.snippet: BBC Verify has been analysing messages after flights across Europe were targeted by fake bomb threats - the second such incident this week.

entries.title: Israel's Arab-led parties in spotlight after inconclusive election
entries.snippet: Israel's center-right opposition has a chance to unseat Netanyahu — but backing of Arab-led parties will be key.

entries.title: The incoming class of U.S. senators is full of historic firsts
entries.snippet: From the first Native American woman elected to the U.S. Senate and the first Muslim who will join the upper chamber to the Senate's first Paralympian, voters elected historic candidates on Tuesday.

entries.title: Trump's global health strategy is emerging. What will the Democratic Congress say?
entries.snippet: The Trump Administration has ushered in a fundamental shift in the U.S. approach to global health aid. How will the newly elected Democratic Congress weigh in?

entries.title: No one knows how many ballots are outstanding in Mississippi's Senate race
entries.snippet: The razor-thin margin between GOP Sen. Cindy Hyde-Smith and Democrat Scott Colom is shining a light on an election process in Mississippi that is among the slowest and most decentralized in the U.S.

entries.title: Stephen Miller will replace Susie Wiles as Trump's chief of staff
entries.snippet: The change comes after sweeping Republican losses in the midterm elections.

entries.title: Pope Leo begins a 12-day, 3-country South America tour after his cancer surgery
entries.snippet: Pope Leo begins his first South American tour since lung cancer surgery. The 12-day journey takes him to Uruguay, Argentina and Peru, where he spent two decades.

entries.title: Health intel-sharing group warns industry in wake of cyberattack on French blood bank
entries.snippet: A healthcare intelligence-sharing organization is warning its members to lock down systems following cyberattacks on cold storage systems, including a French blood bank.

entries.title: Remembering 'Star Trek' actor Patrick Stewart
entries.snippet: Stewart, who died Oct. 28, performed with the Royal Shakespeare Company before becoming famous as Star Trek's Picard. Critic David Bianculli has a tribute, and we listen back to a 2020 interview.

entries.title: European flights and broadcasters are targeted with another wave of bomb threats
entries.snippet: Officials across Europe reported a slew of bomb threats against multiple flights, following a string of hoaxes that caused flight diversions this week. Three broadcasters also received threats.

entries.title: The leader of a Kenyan doomsday cult is sentenced to 200 years in prison
entries.snippet: Cult leader Paul Mackenzie was convicted of murdering 190 children and one adult after he ordered his followers to starve themselves to death in order to meet Jesus.

entries.title: What Trump picking Stephen Miller for chief of staff signals about his agenda
entries.snippet: Trump has replaced White House chief of staff Susie Wiles with Stephen Miller, the hardline architect of his immigration agenda, after a crushing midterm defeat. Immigration, once a political strength for Trump, became a liability after two years of mass detentions, deportations

entries.title: News Wrap: Judge blocks construction of Trump's triumphal arch for now

entries.snippet: Employers added 165,000 new jobs in October, according to a new government report. Job gains for August and September were revised upward as well, by a combined 84,000 jobs. That makes the last three months of the job market look better than expected, but it comes as questions gr

entries.title: Sen.-elect Hamilton reflects on why Kansas voters chose a Democrat for U.S. Senate
entries.snippet: Democrats' midterm wins have reached red states across the country, including Kansas, which has not sent a Democrat to the U.S. Senate since 1932. That will soon change after Rev. Adam Hamilton, who leads the largest United Methodist church in the country, defeated Republican inc

entries.title: Georgia Gov.-elect Bottoms reflects on historic victory and the path forward for Democrats
entries.snippet: Georgia voters made history this week, electing Keisha Lance Bottoms as the state's first Democratic senator in more than two decades and the first-ever Black woman governor in the country. The former Atlanta mayor campaigned on lowering costs, expanding healthcare access and pus

entries.title: Former Sen. Flake, outspoken Trump critic, on the GOP reckoning post-midterms
entries.snippet: As Democrats celebrate their historic gains, Republicans are beginning to take stock of major upsets and what comes next for their party. Amna Nawaz speaks with former Arizona Sen. Jeff Flake, one of the most outspoken Republican critics of Trump during his first administration a

entries.title: Brooks and Capehart on Trump's White House shakeup and fallout from the midterms
entries.snippet: David Brooks of The Atlantic and Jonathan Capehart of MS NOW join Geoff Bennett to discuss the week in politics, including Trump shaking up his White House leadership, deep divisions in the Republican Party and how Democrats are preparing to take control of Congress.

entries.title: Remembering Jay Rockefeller's life and legacy of public service
entries.snippet: Jay Rockefeller, former West Virginia governor and longtime U.S. senator, has died at age 89. Born into one of America's wealthiest and most prominent families, Rockefeller forged his own path in politics and became a leading voice on healthcare, education and the needs of workin

entries.title: Seeds and preserved hair in tomb point to oldest signs of cannabis high 2,800 years ago, study suggests
entries.snippet: Archaeologists who led a dig at a monumental tomb in Siberia said they turned up evidence of the earliest known use of cannabis for psychoactive purposes.

entries.title: Dad of 20-year-old co-pilot in Florida jet crash says her final radio calls showed 'she's tough'
entries.snippet: "I wanted to be by her side," Allan Filgueiras, a pilot who helped teach his daughter to fly, said at a news conference Friday, at times holding back tears. "Inside the plane. To help."

entries.title: Cornell faculty vote 'no confidence' in university leadership after alleged fraternity gang rape
entries.snippet: While the faculty body has no power over the university's top leaders, backers of the resolution had said they hoped it would pressure Cornell's trustees to address longstanding institutional failures they identified.

entries.title: Democrats win the Arizona House, Senate and governor's office for the first time since 1966
entries.snippet: The Associated Press called enough legislative races to confirm that both chambers flipped on Friday.

entries.title: WATCH: 'Elections matter.' Houston mayor limits police cooperation with ICE
entries.snippet: The shift in the nation's fourth-largest city is one of the first actions to restrict U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement operations since Democrats' rout in Tuesday's midterm elections.

entries.title: Trump's triumphal arch is blocked for now, but a new website highlights the plans
entries.snippet: The White House highlighted the website the morning after U.S. District Judge Tanya Chutkan issued a temporary restraining order that prohibits work on the site for 14 days.

entries.title: Connecticut Sen. Chris Murphy released from hospital after stroke
entries.snippet: The 53-year-old Democrat said in a statement Friday that doctors are "encouraged by the progress" he's made so far.

entries.title: Schumer says Democrats will stop Trump from placing 'right-winger' on the Supreme Court
entries.snippet: Schumer says the party's agenda will center around lowering prices, along with five issues that they have focused on in the minority — healthcare, housing, Trump's tariffs, childcare and lowering energy bills.

entries.title: Trump names Stephen Miller his next chief of staff after major Republican midterm losses
entries.snippet: President Trump's White House chief of staff, Susie Wiles, is stepping down. She is Trump's longest-serving chief of staff and the first woman ever to hold the position.

entries.title: Latino voters propel Democrats to big wins with leftward swing
entries.snippet: Hispanic voters, especially those in the working class, have been impacted by economic challenges, leading them to reject President Donald Trump and his Republican Party.

entries.title: 3 charged in $129 million AI scheme targeting thousands of companies
entries.snippet: Their victims included hospital systems in Missouri and California, a bank in Rhode Island, a financial technology company in the United Kingdom, a mutual fund company in Massachusetts and a pet food company in Florida, according to court documents.

entries.title: Online magazine Salon announces it is shutting down
entries.snippet: Salon said there were no immediate plans to take down its online archives, which include three decades of stories from across the world and across topics and genres.

entries.title: DW
entries.snippet: News, Analysis and Service from Germany and Europe - in 30 Languages

entries.title: Pope Leo arrives in Uruguay at start of South America tour
entries.snippet: Pope Leo has arrived in Uruguay at the start of a 12-day trip through three South American nations. His trip, which is intense with a packed itinerary, comes just weeks after his lung cancer surgery.

entries.title: Tankers carrying Russian diesel to the US change course
entries.snippet: Despite an ostensible deal between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin to bring diesel to the US, tankers are reportedly unable to dock due to existing sanctions.

entries.title: Stephen Miller named by Trump as new White House chief of staff
entries.snippet: Trump said he would be replacing Susie Wiles for the top advisory role. Miller is controversial figure, known as a key architect of the administration's hardline immigration policies.

entries.title: Ueno Bank scandal plunges Paraguay into political crisis
entries.snippet: Suspected financial fraud, public money at risk and millions of customers affected: Paraguay is in serious crisis following the sudden collapse of Ueno Bank. President Santiago Pena is facing impeachment.

entries.title: Critics say Democrats should look into Trump's Middle East deals in future corruption investigations
entries.snippet: After their victory in the US midterm elections, the Democrats have promised to investigate corruption in the Trump administration. Critics say the president's Middle East deals is an area they should focus on.

entries.title: Ilse Aigner tipped by party allies as next German president
entries.snippet: German media reports suggest that Bavarian politician Ilse Aigner's chances of becoming the next president are on the up. Long favored by her Bavarian CSU, now it seems Christian Democrats nationwide plan to back her.

entries.title: Meghan Markle's father arrested in US over child sex abuse material
entries.snippet: US federal agents arrested Thomas Markle in Florida. The Duchess of Sussex and television actress Meghan Markle, who is estranged from her father, said she was "deeply distressed" by the charges.

entries.title: Iran war: Gulf tanker attacked, 1 seaferer killed
entries.snippet: Iran is stepping up attacks on shipping in the Persian Gulf and Strait of Hormuz. A Greek-owned tanker believed to have been struck with a missile, and Iran said two other vessels were on fire.

entries.title: Tesla to 'wind down' production of flop Cybertruck
entries.snippet: Elon Musk's electric pickup for the future will start to be consigned to the past next year. The Cybertruck's bulk and crude shape meant it could only pass regulatory standards in more permissive markets.

entries.title: Data center protesters break into Microsoft site in Amsterdam
entries.snippet: Protesters are demanding a pause in data center construction in Europe. Campaigners planning protests in 16 countries say the AI building boom threatens water supplies, power grids and climate goals.

entries.title: Despite Russia impasse, Germany still hoping to host Men's Ice Hockey World Championship
entries.snippet: A week after a court ruled that Russia must be allowed to return to international ice hockey, the way forward remains unclear. Berlin is seeking a solution that will allow Germany to host next year's Word Championship.

entries.title: Germany: Small plane crashes onto A2 highway, killing 2
entries.snippet: Two people have died after a small plane crashed onto Germany's A2 highway near Magdeburg. The crash closed the Hannover-bound lanes on a major east-west route, with no road vehicles reported to be involved.

entries.title: Fact check: Three viral Iran war posts debunked
entries.snippet: After Monday's US attack on Iran, social media is awash with dramatic images and claims about renewed fighting. DW Fact Check found AI-generated and recycled videos — as well as misleading posts from dubious accounts.

entries.title: Protests and reforms: France's rising debt costs threaten stability
entries.snippet: France plans to spend an extra €4 billion on education amid nationwide protests. But with public debt mounting and interest costs climbing, how much fiscal room does the government have?

entries.title: Czech arms makers set sights on space defense in bid to sustain Ukraine-driven arms boom
entries.snippet: Czech arms makers have thrived on demand linked to the war in Ukraine. To sustain their growth, they need to look beyond ammunition and toward new technologies — and even space.

entries.title: Zambia's civil service overhaul raises questions
entries.snippet: Government-backed retirements and institutional realignments are fueling debate in Zambia, with opposition politicians questioning transparency while officials defend the changes as necessary reforms.

entries.title: What to know about the IIHF Women's Ice Hockey World Championship
entries.snippet: As ice hockey's governing body continues to wrangle over how to respond to a CAS order to reinstate Russia to international play, the top women's tournament gets underway in Denmark without Russia.

entries.title: Global temperatures are set to exceed 1.5 degrees above pre-industrial levels in 2026, likely the second-warmest year on record
entries.snippet: Climate scientists say the world is set to breach the critical 1.5-degree Celsius threshold in 2026. This year is also on track to become the second-warmest on record.

entries.title: For people in Iran, a constant threat of war and dearth of information
entries.snippet: Most people in Iran have little idea of the course of the US-led war and peace talks on the global stage. With few sources of information, the population must navigate conflicting rumors and fears of a nuclear attack.
